ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit in the attached figure, the upper wire is the signal node, and the lower wire is the reference ground. The left side is labeled input voltage vi(t), and the right side is labeled output voltage vo(t). Between the input node and the output node there is a parallel RC branch: the upper part is a 1 kΩ resistor, and the lower part is a 4 μF capacitor. Between the output node and ground there is also a parallel RC branch: a 4 kΩ resistor and a 1 μF capacitor are connected in parallel. The problem states that all capacitors are initially uncharged. Reasoning: Since the capacitors are initially uncharged, there is no need to add initial-condition sources in the s domain. Denote the parallel RC branch between the input and output as Z1, then Z1 = 1 kΩ || 1/(s·4 μF) = 1000/(1 + 0.004s). Denote the parallel RC branch between the output node and ground as Z2, then Z2 = 4 kΩ || 1/(s·1 μF) = 4000/(1 + 0.004s). In the s domain, this circuit is a voltage-divider structure of Z1 and Z2, so Vo(s) = Vi(s)·Z2/(Z1 + Z2). The input vi(t)=10u(t), therefore Vi(s)=10/s. Substituting gives Vo(s) = (10/s)·[4000/(1+0.004s)] / {[1000/(1+0.004s)] + [4000/(1+0.004s)]}. The common factor 1/(1+0.004s) in the numerator and denominator cancels, obtaining Vo(s) = (10/s)·4000/5000 = 8/s. Taking the inverse Laplace transform gives vo(t)=8u(t) V.
